answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and incumbent's refusal to reopen price make renegotiation unviable. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and reliable invoicing—the operational conditions that matter at 94% line utilization. memory_c4 shows renegotiation has already been exhausted this cycle. However, given the 14-day window and zero buffer in committed volume, a small guarded test with the low-cost vendor is prudent: qualify them on a subset volume, verify quality and lead times under current demand stress, then escalate to primary if confidence builds. This preserves the option to revert to incumbent or add second source (memory_c3) if onboarding reveals risk, while pursuing the cost target the business has mandated. The tight timeline and high line utilization create real downstream value risk if the new vendor stumbles, so guardrails matter more than speed.
